also: strong (of a feeling, heat or pain)

evidence: Plin. NH 24.62: dolor capitis vehementior (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 17.235: vīs frīgorum aut calōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of pain, rain, heat, cold, a blow or a feeling: strong, powerful; of a person, vehement, violent. The adverb vehementer is the everyday “very much, intensely” (vehementer gaudeō).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.183: ācer et vehemēns incitātiō (Lewis & Short, s.v. vehemēns)
terms.comment: Sharp to the senses (a piercing cold, a pungent taste), keen in mind, fierce in battle; intense in that it bites.

evidence: Cic. Fl. 11 (Lewis & Short, s.v. intendō): quam maximē intentīs … oculīs contemplārī
Verg. A. 2.1: intentī ōra tenēbant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Intense attention or effort: intentus with the dative or ablative of what one is intent on; intentissima cūra, the most intense care (Quint.).

phrases.latin: cōnsonant vehementer, proinde ut mīlitēs faciunt, cum castra movent
phrases.english: they hum loudly, just as soldiers do when they break camp
I’m watching with all my attention.
